problem_statement: A generic utility function is needed to count the number of set bits in a byte array of arbitrary length. The function should accept a pointer to a value and its size in bytes, and return the total number of set bits across all bytes. It should use a hardware popcount instruction when available, and otherwise fall back to a portable byte-by-bit algorithm. Several subsystems (Bluetooth audio, ADC driver, kernel bitarray tests) currently have their own local bit-counting implementations that should be replaced by this shared function.
twister_command: scripts/twister -p qemu_x86 -T tests/kernel/common -s tests/kernel/common/kernel.common -s kernel.common -O twister-out --no-clean -W

verification.reason: The task can be made fair by adding the public API name, header, and signature; no unrepairable implementation detail is required.

problems.detail: The statement does not name the required API sys_count_bits, but the hidden tests call it by that name.
The statement does not state that sys_count_bits must be available from <zephyr/sys/util.h>, which the unit test includes and the other tests rely on through that interface.
The statement does not give the exact signature and return type the tests rely on: size_t sys_count_bits(const void *value, size_t len).

problem_statement_fixed: A generic utility function, sys_count_bits, is needed and must be visible to code that includes <zephyr/sys/util.h>. It should have the signature size_t sys_count_bits(const void *value, size_t len), accept a pointer to a value and its size in bytes, and return the total number of set bits across all bytes. It should use a hardware popcount instruction when available, and otherwise fall back to a portable byte-by-bit algorithm. Several subsystems (Bluetooth audio, ADC driver, kernel bitarray tests) currently have their own local bit-counting implementations that should be replaced by this shared function.
